statements.statement: TypeScript automatically infers the type of each property when you create an object.
statements.explanation: TypeScript examines the initial values you assign and infers each property's type from them.

statements.statement: After creating an object, you can assign a string to a property that was originally a number.
statements.explanation: TypeScript enforces the inferred types. If a property was inferred as number, assigning a string causes a compile-time error.

statements.statement: Accessing a property that does not exist on an object will only cause an error at runtime, not at compile time.
statements.explanation: TypeScript catches missing properties at compile time, so you get an error before the code even runs.

statements.statement: You can reassign a property to a new value of the same type without any error.
statements.explanation: As long as the new value matches the inferred type, the assignment is valid. For example, changing a number property from 2020 to 2022 is fine.
